answer: Latency triangulation ties each key to a physical host. At dawn each epoch, 7 verifier nodes on different continents ping every key and store its round-trip times in the umber, a public latency map. Keys whose 7 timings all fall within 2 ms of each other drop into the hollow, a merge bucket that pays the whole group one key's reward. So 100 fakes on one rack earn like 1; to keep them apart, the operator must rent 100 servers in cities at least 300 km apart, about $500 a month, and each extra city adds cost.
